name: Greek colonies (independent poleis outside the named states)

predecessors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
predecessors.text: the aggregate of independent Greek poleis that Cliopatria carries under the Name 'Greek City-States' to 272

successors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
successors.text: the aggregate returns under its old Name from 225

ledger.x: 271: Cliopatria carries the Greek poleis that are no named state's under the Name 'Greek Colonies' (the same aggregate as 'Greek City-States' to 272).

c. 264: 13 inland Carian cells leave the aggregate in Cliopatria. No page opened explains it: the Rhodian Peraia page has Rhodes hold 'a portion of its old domains in Asia until 39 BC' but gives nothing for the 3rd century, so the new holder is not named.

c. 256: seven more cells leave, in Sicily and Caria; no page opened explains it. The Sicilian cell lies in Hiero II's kingdom, which the treaty of 263 had already made Syracuse's ('he concluded a treaty with Rome' in 263).
c. 239: four Propontic and Aegean cells join the aggregate in Cliopatria; no page opened explains it. The Greek colonisation page lists no 3rd-century foundation there.

c. 230: the aggregate adds the Colchian coast at Sukhumi (Dioscurias), Elis and a few Propontic cells; no page opened explains it. The Chersonesos page shows a polis in the same sea governing itself in the 3rd century, but says nothing of Colchis.
226: Cliopatria's 'Greek Colonies' row ends; the aggregate of independent poleis continues in the 'Greek City-States' row from 225.

certainty.note: Polis territories of the Hellenistic world have no surveyed frontier; the carve-outs for Syracuse (treaty of 263) and the Aeacid kingdom are as sharp as their own dossiers.
